advices.diagnosis: The class exhibits low cohesion (LCOM4=2) because its methods operate on two distinct clusters of attributes: one cluster uses `self._width` for formatting (`title`, `describe_customer`), while the other cluster uses `self._repository` and `self._mailer` for data retrieval and communication (`order_count`, `mail_summary`). Additionally, `describe_customer` displays feature envy by accessing four attributes of the `Customer` object, suggesting that the formatting logic for customer details might belong elsewhere or that the method is doing too much for a view component.

suggestions.title: Extract formatting logic into a dedicated Formatter class
suggestions.sketch: Create a `ReportFormatter` class that holds the `_width` attribute and contains the `title` and `describe_customer` methods. `ReportView` would then delegate these calls to an instance of `ReportFormatter`. This separates the presentation logic (formatting) from the data access logic (repository/mailer), reducing the number of connected components in the method-attribute graph of `ReportView`.

suggestions.title: Move customer description logic to Customer or a CustomerPresenter
suggestions.sketch: The `describe_customer` method accesses `customer.customer_id()`, `customer.name()`, `customer.email()`, and `customer.tier()`. This is a classic case of feature envy. Moving this logic to a `Customer` method (e.g., `customer.format_for_report()`) or a dedicated `CustomerPresenter` would reduce the dependency of `ReportView` on the internal structure of `Customer` and improve cohesion by grouping related data access and formatting together.

advices.risk_notes: Extracting the formatter increases the number of classes in the system (DCC up) and may introduce indirection that complicates simple use cases. Moving customer description logic to the domain model (`Customer`) might violate layering rules if the domain model should remain free of presentation concerns (like string formatting with specific widths). If `Customer` is a shared domain object, adding view-specific formatting methods to it could be a design smell. The first suggestion (extracting formatter) is generally safer and more aligned with the Single Responsibility Principle.
